metadata.description: Stride task management skills for AI agents

plugins.name: stride
plugins.description: Drive the full Stride kanban task lifecycle from Claude Code — claiming, completing, creating and enriching tasks and goals, workflow orchestration, subagent dispatch, and automatic lifecycle hook execution, with optional gated integrations for exploratory manual testing, hardening findings into drafted regression checks, and deep security-considerations review. New in v1.63.0: opt-in per-task context isolation. G404 shrank the resident skill body; this targets the other half of the cost — what each task accumulates in the main loop (the diff, the explorer/planner/reviewer reports, the hook tails), all re-sent on every later main-loop request while nothing fails and nothing looks wrong. Adds docs/task-runner-contract.md, the schema of record for both directions of the handoff: inbound is six fields, each admitted only by passing one stated test (the runner cannot obtain it from GET /api/tasks/:id), and outbound is an eleven-field record under a 4,000-byte cap bracketed by a measured saturated maximum of 3,509 B and a compounding ceiling of 4,026 B, so no schema-conforming record can breach it. Bounds are stated in UTF-8 bytes of the serialised value rather than characters, deliberately — under character bounds a conforming record carrying CJK or escape-heavy text could reach four figures past the cap. Adds agents/task-runner.md, which owns one task claim-through-complete, dispatches its own explorer, planner and reviewer rather than inlining them, and returns only the bounded record. Adds Step 1.5 dispatcher mode, gated exactly like Steps 5.5/5.6 with its body in optional-dispatcher-mode.md loaded only when the gate fires, so the resident body grows 7.2 KB rather than by the whole procedure; Steps 2-8 are not moved or deleted, and dispatcher mode says only who executes them. Adds an isolation size gate on the Step 3 matrix, derived rather than asserted: a dispatch re-pays a fixed ~92,000-token base that does not shrink with the task, while the saving scales with what the task accumulates, whose largest component is subagent reports at 6,261 tokens each — which a small 0-1 key_files task produces none of. The after_goal PATCH now has a named owner per branch, because the bundle rides on /complete in one branch and /mark_reviewed in the other; assigning it wholly to the runner would have left a goal's last child with needs_review=true ownerless, and the grace worker flips such a goal to Done without pushing. Also moves the verified subagent hook behaviour into hook-execution.md with the method behind each claim, retracting the incorrect claim that a subagent may read silence from a gate as a pass — its own negative control is the counter-example, since a hook that never fired is equally silent. Shipped incomplete, deliberately: the end-to-end verification run and the token measurement that depends on it are NOT in this release, because both need stride:task-runner installed rather than sitting in a working tree. Dispatcher mode is therefore opt-in and unexercised end to end — it changes nothing for a session that does not ask for it, which is why shipping it now is safe, but it should not be treated as proven until those two tasks run. New in v1.64.0: a completing task's `changed_files` now carries the commits **that task** made rather than everything committed between its claim and its completion (nested tasks no longer bleed into an outer task's diff — the normal shape under dispatcher mode); the hook executor emits **exactly one JSON document** on stdout, so harness-facing fields such as `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` are actually read instead of being dropped by a failed strict parse whenever a primary section and `## after_goal` both ran; every hook section that does work persists its structured result to `.stride/.hook-result-<hook>.json`, making `after_goal`'s real duration readable for its follow-up PATCH; a `"failed"` section verdict must now carry a substantive note (rejected outright if it is a stub or a bare restatement of the status); and both hook test suites calibrate machine load and scale their wall-clock backstops — clamped below each case's un-killed duration — so their failure count no longer depends on what else the machine is doing. New in v1.65.0: a skipped `workflow_steps` entry may carry an optional machine-readable `reason_code` beside its free-text `reason` — six values derived by classifying every skipped entry on a real board (73 entries had produced 58 distinct prose strings averaging 145 characters), optional and omittable so agents that predate it complete unchanged, with `matrix_deviation` reserved for a step the decision matrix actually called for; and all three report-producing agents move to write-then-summarise — `task-reviewer` persists its structured block and human report to `.stride/`, `task-explorer` and the generic `Plan` dispatch persist their full findings there too, each returning a bounded summary naming the path (24 lines / 2,000 characters for the reviewer, a deliberately looser 60 lines / 6,000 characters for the explorer and planner, whose summaries are implemented from rather than parsed), with a dispatch that supplies no path writing nothing and emitting inline so older orchestrators keep working, and consumers reading only the paths they themselves supplied. New in v1.66.0: the hot path is re-extracted and size-gated. G404's saving had been eaten silently in four days — the orchestrator skill regrew from 80,523 to 119,880 bytes — so this release reverses the regrowth and makes a third occurrence impossible: stride-workflow/SKILL.md returns to 89,647 bytes with the regrown material moved to gated sibling files (review-block extraction mechanics, the deep security-considerations procedure, the behaviour_test_matrix contract, the hook-duration derivation, the Step 3 design rationale), every gate, decision matrix, Decision Summary and prompt-injection framing rule kept inline and each moved block reachable from a pointer at its original site; stride-completing-tasks/SKILL.md gets the same pass (100,085 to 56,750 bytes, the Field Reference / result schema / skip-reason enum / pre-submission hard gate / curl stdout rules staying inline, with the session-text redaction rules moving WITH their point of use into manual-testing-findings.md), re-verified against the server contract with no field requirement, schema shape or enum value changed; and scripts/check-skill-budgets.sh runs as hook-suite Group 28 with budgets 12-13% above post-extraction sizes (drift detectors, not targets), its failure naming the file, size, budget, extraction pattern and the budget table's location. Slim views are adopted where they pay: the index/tree GET curls carry response_view=slim (the bare index measured 2.4 MB / ~840,000 tokens against production; slim is roughly 1% of that), the complete curl adopts the slim acknowledgement (correctness on Claude Code, ~22,000 tokens per completion on non-truncating runtimes), dispatcher mode's capture-and-project workaround becomes a projected fields=status,needs_review show read, and the plugin's prose is reconciled with the shipped server capability with an explicit older-server caveat at every conditioned site — while claim and next deliberately stay full. reference.md's dispatcher summaries gain the completed-status confirmation gate (completed loops only after the projected read agrees; a disagreement or failed read is abandoned/unparseable_record, report and stop), and its deference note now names the gated step files as winning on any disagreement., and (v1.67.0+) progressive disclosure for the three largest agent bodies — `task-reviewer` 66,177→55,936, `task-enricher` 37,338→28,865 and `task-decomposer` 25,521→13,684 bytes, **30,551 bytes** off the per-dispatch cost — with only worked examples, edge-case sections and anti-example galleries moved to sibling `docs/` files and every contract kept inline (the emitted block schema, the verdict rules, the bounded-summary contract, the four enrichment phases and their field types, the six decomposition steps and both sizing tables, and in all three the prompt-injection framing and the redaction rules), placed in `docs/` rather than `agents/` because every `.md` there registers as a dispatchable agent; each split verified by dispatching the slimmed body against a real fixture rather than by reading the diff, which is what caught a returned-summary rendering that existed only in the example being moved, a waived-matrix-row shape stated only by a sentence narrating that example, and a decomposer that never carried a treat-task-text-as-data boundary at all despite consuming free-form human goal text; the decomposer's duplicated request envelope is deleted rather than moved, pointing at the `stride-creating-goals` skill that owns it; plus the commit-attribution lineage closing — per-window purity classification (D244), hook-mediated commit ownership (D255), the purity fixpoint so concurrent siblings cannot manufacture purity (D256), per-window open-window-aware eviction so a live outer's anchor never falls to the cap (D268), the outermost-task gate that stops a silent under-report (D271), and the zero-commit-child ratchet pinned rather than fixed after the candidate branch was measured breaking nine pre-existing pins (D272) — and a relatedness gate ahead of the Step 5.5 severity/provenance policy, so a finding whose responsible lines are lines this task changed is fixed in-task at any severity rather than filed (D270) filed (D270), and (v1.68.0+) a confirmed command-injection fix and the end of the native-Windows capture gap — `stride-hook.ps1` wrote server-supplied values bare into the env cache that `stride-hook.sh` `source`s under `set -a`, so a crafted task title executed at source time (D280, confirmed executing; every writer now escapes, the loader unquotes with an exact inverse, and the shell-steering fence is an allow-list) — while the ps1 hook, which previously had no capture step and so produced no snapshot at all on native Windows, now builds it and runs the same classification, per-window eviction and narrowing-replay engine as bash (W2100–W2106, ps1 suite 530 → 961); on Windows PowerShell 5.1 the diff still cannot upload and after_goal detection is a silent no-op, both from one 7-only parameter at two call sites (D277), and the hook has never been executed under `powershell.exe` (D237). v1.69.0+: a canonical cross-port rules document (`docs/port-canon.md`) and a drift check that turns it into an enforced contract (`scripts/check-port-canon.sh`), covering five rules across the port fleet with per-port applicability recorded as data rather than prose, plus the four canon anchors adopted in this port and a documented release-time step so the canon cannot ship half-synced. v1.70.0+: six hook-executor defects closed, four of them silent data-loss paths that produced a success-shaped result — a non-ASCII path lost its entire diff, a long single-line diff burned the whole after_doing budget in a quadratic line counter, the hook-env key filter became an allow-list over the 17 documented names, a PowerShell 7-only parameter meant the changed_files PUT never issued on 5.1, env-cache writes became byte-preserving so a ps1 write no longer destroys unrelated records, and a compare-and-swap stops a record write discarding a concurrent claim., and (v1.71.0+) all four follow-ups filed at 1.70.0 closed, plus D287 and the PowerShell canon-check twin — a server-supplied `TASK_TITLE` carrying a record-shaped line no longer forges another task's snapshot anchor, because records are identified by where they *begin* rather than by a line-oriented match (**D287**); the Windows dirty-baseline listing gains `-z`, so the pre-existing-edit filter stops being silently inert for every non-ASCII path (**D286**); the `changed_files` upload filter fails **closed**, where a `catch` had recovered by uploading the raw unfiltered bytes — measured putting `.stride_auth.md` on the wire (**D290**); the bash env-cache filters drop `grep` for `index`/`substr` on the ASCII key and propagate their exit status, so a contributor's binary-refusing `grep` can no longer empty the cache at exit 0 — measured on a real refusing `grep` in both its shapes, and awk's regex engine turned out to abort on the same byte (**D288**); the five remaining `Write-EnvCache` callers move behind one shared compare-and-swap helper (**D289**); and `scripts/check-port-canon.ps1` gives the drift check a PowerShell half written as an independent implementation rather than a transliteration, with both halves' self-tests wired into both suites and a cross-check comparing their case-name sets — which caught three divergences invisible to a fleet-wide diff (**W2107**). New in v1.72.0: two gates stop reporting a subject clean without looking at it — the reviewer could never return `approved` on a task with a commit criterion, and two canon cells were excluded from every check while the run exited 0 — the three curl invocation rules become a PreToolUse gate rather than prose that had already failed under load, and eleven commits converge the two halves of the port-canon drift check, which had returned opposite verdicts on a NUL-bearing canon and blocked forever on a named pipe (**W2127**, **D302**, **W2131**, **D285**, **D293**–**D299**)

plugins.name: stride-security-review
plugins.description: AI-powered security review via /stride-security-review:security-review. Two scan modes: diff (default, PR-gating) and --full (codebase posture check, batched with cross-batch dedup and skipped-files reporting). Detects 10 universal vulnerability classes plus 5 MAESTRO-derived agentic-AI classes (prompt injection, tool abuse, agent trust boundary, model output execution, vector-store poisoning). Seven framework rule packs (new in 2.3.0): Android/Kotlin (exported components, WebView JS bridge RCE, cleartext traffic, SharedPreferences credentials, SQLite injection, trust-all SSL), Django/Python (mark_safe, raw/extra SQL, CSRF, production settings, mass-assignment, open-redirect, deserialization, SSRF, DRF mass-assignment), Express/Node.js (reflected XSS, eval RCE, child_process injection, Mongoose NoSQL injection, prototype pollution), iOS/Swift (UserDefaults credentials, WKWebView file access, ATS arbitrary loads, URLSession trust-all, deep-link missing auth), Phoenix/Elixir (raw/1, force_ssl, CSRF, fragment interpolation, LiveView scope, mass-assignment, Token replay, System.cmd shell, LiveView upload guards, open-redirect), Rails/Ruby (html_safe, find_by_sql, CSRF, params.permit!, eval/send, open-redirect, deserialization, connection.execute, missing-auth, JSON-leak), React/Next.js (dangerouslySetInnerHTML, API route missing auth, redirect open-redirect, javascript: href scheme, getServerSideProps secret leak). Plus a multi-platform CI/CD pipeline pack (8 platforms) and a framework-agnostic Web defense-in-depth pack covering security headers (CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options/cookie flags). Every finding carries CWE-ID and OWASP Top 10 references. Opt-in flags: --maestro (7-layer threat classification with explicit non-AI mapping), --rci [N] (recursive criticism passes), --baseline (suppress acknowledged findings), --patches (surgical-fix unified diffs), --fail-on <severity> (CI exit-code gate), --base <ref> (PR-against-base diff scope), --sarif (SARIF v2.1.0 output for GitHub Code Scanning), --considerations <source> (considerations mode, new in 2.5.0 — verifies a task's security_considerations were actually mitigated by the diff via a per-consideration mitigated/partial/unmitigated verdict, byte-identical output when not set). Ships a reference GitHub Actions workflow and a TAP 13 eval runner over 72 fixtures with positive-and-negative-control coverage (including considerations-mode controls), plus golden-file tests for the deterministic SARIF/dedup/fingerprint/fail-on transforms (new in 2.4.0). Semantic analysis, not pattern matching. Loosely based on anthropics/claude-code-security-review.

plugins.name: stride-ideation
plugins.description: Turn a fuzzy idea into shipped Stride tasks via two slash commands — /ideate drives an interactive, profile-aware question loop that hard-gates seven requirements sections into a committed markdown doc, and /stridify decomposes that doc into Stride goals and tasks via the batch API.

plugins.name: stride-lite
plugins.description: Lightweight companion plugin to Stride — produces Stride-shaped goal and task markdown documents on disk from a free-text prompt plus an optional requirements directory. No API calls, no kanban setup, no auth files. Just markdown. Useful when you want the Stride field discipline (acceptance criteria, key files, pitfalls, testing strategy, dependencies) without committing to the full Stride server workflow — the documents it produces can be reviewed, edited, or later submitted to a real Stride deployment by hand or by tooling, but this plugin never does so itself. Surface: three slash commands and one workflow skill. /stride-lite:create-goal decomposes a prompt into a goal directory with one goal.md plus 1–8 child taskN.md files; /stride-lite:create-task renders a single task markdown file; /stride-lite:init scaffolds a project-local .stride_lite.md with email plus three hook sections (## before_task, ## after_task, ## after_goal). The stride-lite-workflow skill is the file-based equivalent of the full Stride plugin's stride-workflow — it walks a goal directory through an eight-step task lifecycle (select → before_task → explore → implement → after_task → review → review-loop decision → completion + archive), dispatching the two read-only subagents at the right moments. Three subagents are shipped: stride-lite:create-decomposer (decomposes a free-text prompt into a goal + child tasks YAML, no API calls), stride-lite:task-explorer (read-only enrichment with codebase context — Read / Grep / Glob, no Bash, no WebFetch; appends ## Exploration Report), and stride-lite:task-reviewer (reviews changes against acceptance criteria, pitfalls, patterns, and testing strategy with narrowly-scoped read-only git Bash; appends ## Review Report with embedded reviewer_result JSON, schema 1.1). v0.9.0+: hooks/hooks.json registers Claude Code PreToolUse/PostToolUse handlers that auto-fire the three .stride_lite.md sections at the corresponding workflow intercepts — ## before_task before the task-explorer Agent dispatch (blocking, exit 2 stops the dispatch), ## after_task before the task-reviewer Agent dispatch (blocking, exit 2 stops the dispatch), ## after_goal after the goal.md Edit/Write that appends ## Completion Summary (advisory — PostToolUse cannot roll back the write). Cross-platform from day one: hooks/stride-lite-hook.sh (POSIX bash, pure-bash JSON parsing, no jq dependency) and hooks/stride-lite-hook.ps1 (PowerShell 5.1+, ConvertFrom-Json / ConvertTo-Json, no module installs); the .sh script auto-delegates to .ps1 on native Windows (OSTYPE unset + COMSPEC set). v0.10.0+: stride-lite-workflow Step 8 final-task branch performs a terminal PENDING → IMPLEMENTED archive move — after ## after_goal fires, the goal directory moves from docs/implementation/PENDING/<slug>/ to docs/implementation/IMPLEMENTED/<slug>/ via git mv when tracked (preserves rename history) or plain mv otherwise. Collision suffixing on the target with -2 / -3 / … up to a 1000-iteration safety cap (never overwrites), after-goal-failure no-move guard (a structured failed-status JSON from the harness skips the move so the user can re-trigger), non-/PENDING/ path skip with a stderr warning (custom --output-dir is left where it is), and clean exit on filesystem-mv failure (logged, the workflow does not fail because of an archive-move failure). Single-task files under PENDING/tasks/ are NEVER moved — only goal directories. v0.11.0+: copy installs ship the hook enforcement layer — install.sh previously copied every directory except hooks/, so script-based installs silently lacked the documented auto-fire entirely (pre-0.11.0 copy installs should re-run ./install.sh --force); the installer now copies hooks/ with the executable bit preserved, reports it in the summary, and fails loudly if hooks.json does not land. Also: the init surface, workflow walkthrough, and scaffolded template all teach the v0.9.0 harness-executes model (the stale static-config and workflow-skill-executes claims are gone), phantom /stride-lite:ideate//stride-lite:decompose references are purged with the decomposer's unjustified Read/Grep grant removed, the smoke suite grows 24 to 43 assertions with machine-enforced init-template parity and nine hook-routing payload fixtures, and the shipped init-command goal artifact is archived PENDING to IMPLEMENTED per the plugin's own convention. v0.12.0+: three optional gated sub-steps in stride-lite-workflow, each dispatching an agent from a DIFFERENT plugin, all skipped cleanly when that plugin is absent and never able to fail a task — Step 6a maps a task's manual-test entries to charters and dispatches stride-exploratory-testing:explorer once per charter with a session budget read from the installed agent's own contract (the authorized-and-non-production affirmative is collected at Step 0 or never; it is never inferred from a localhost URL), Step 6b hardens confirmed findings into regression checks staged outside the test tree and never reported as passing since /harden holds no test runner, and Step 6c dispatches stride-security-review:security-reviewer in explicitly-declared considerations mode for one verdict per listed consideration, fail-closed so a consideration is never marked mitigated on a verdict set that could not be read. Also new: SECURITY.md states the trust boundary (the plugin executes arbitrary user-authored shell commands from .stride_lite.md, unvalidated and unwrapped) and records that the activation marker is a forgeable coordination signal and never an authorization, and that the PowerShell executor has not been verified on a real Windows host; dedicated hook test suites (hooks/test-stride-lite-hook.sh and .ps1) covering the section executor's internals; and Red flags plus Rationalization Table scaffolding across all four skills. Four defects fixed, three of them found by suites this release introduced: the PowerShell executor never received the hook payload at all, reading stdin via @($input) which is empty for the OS-level pipe the harness uses, so the documented auto-fire had never worked on native Windows and exited 0 without reporting it (D215); Start-Process -ArgumentList re-split every command so bash received only its first token, making every multi-word hook command silently do nothing while reporting success (D218); the decision matrix counted only table rows under ## Key files, so a hand-written bullet or numbered list of three real files resolved to skip-all with no explorer, no reviewer and no hooks, while the enrichment gate read the same section as populated (D216); and a three-backtick markdown fence wrapping a three-backtick json block closed early, rendering the rest of an agent contract as sample output — now caught by a fence walk in both backtick and tilde syntax, since neither a fence count nor an unterminated-fence check can see it (D217). v0.13.0+: the task-reviewer prompt now states that `note` is REQUIRED on a `failed` section verdict, matching what the completion API has enforced unconditionally since D231 (D240). v0.14.0+: the branch-selection matrix states that it is the only thing gating explore, plan and review, and states what its first-match reading rule rests on, leading with the precondition that a missing `## Key files` heading resolves to `full` before any row is consulted; the fleet `reason_code` vocabulary is deliberately deferred here and recorded as a deferral rather than adopted.

plugins.name: launchdarkly
plugins.description: Generate correct, testable, and removable LaunchDarkly feature-flag code from Claude Code — covers the Java server SDK and the TypeScript SDKs (Node server, client-side JS, React) with skills, scaffolding and flag-removal commands, and an anti-pattern review agent. v0.3.0+: the client-side skill is modernized to the scoped v4 SDKs (@launchdarkly/js-client-sdk and @launchdarkly/react-sdk with createLDReactProvider and typed hooks, the unscoped v3 packages preserved in a labeled legacy section); /launchdarkly:ld-scaffold gains real browser and react targets (four targets total); the reviewer agent gains eight-plus anti-pattern rules; and the plugin now ships a dependency-free scripts/smoke.sh validation gate.

plugins.name: stride-exploratory-testing
plugins.description: Drive structured, charter-based exploratory testing sessions in Claude Code — the discipline that supplies the "explored" half of Tested = Checked + Explored. Plan charters, run timeboxed sessions against a running app under an absolute safety boundary, judge results with oracles, and capture findings as an SBTM session sheet and debrief. Surface: six skills (stride-exploratory-testing orchestrator, chartering, heuristics, oracles, bug-advocacy, session), seven slash commands (/charter, /nightmare-headline, /explore, /pair, /recon, /debrief, /harden), and two subagents (charter-generator, explorer). Pairs with a human driving the app (/pair), turns confirmed bugs into drafted regression checks in your own test framework (/harden), and persists session artifacts, a charter backlog, and a coverage map under .exploratory/ so findings survive the conversation. Ships worked example fixtures (charter set, session sheet, debrief) and a pure-shell smoke-test harness under lib/. Encodes established exploratory-testing practice — Kaner, Hendrickson's Explore It!, SBTM (Bach), Whittaker's Tours, and Bach's Heuristic Test Strategy Model.
